Programmers can build bias into algorithms by relying on data that they know are biased against a certain racial or religious group, or that reflect historical discrimination. Algorithms can also be affected by the implicit or unconscious bias of the people who program them. In desperate treatment cases, the plaintiff must show that the employer intended to discriminate on the basis of some prohibited characteristic.
